sees: frame 1: A woman with a dark ponytail in a red coat with a shoulder bag stands in front of library bookshelves, looking worried/unhappy with a slight frown, holding a small dark-blue open book at her side.

frame 2: Same woman, eyes half-lidded and flat, mouth neutral (tired or unimpressed). The blue book is now lower, at her bag level, resting just above a small wooden stool that has appeared next to her.
frame 3: Background changed to an office/desk area with computer monitors. The woman looks neutral and slightly wide-eyed. The blue book sits on top of the small wooden stool beside her.
actor: A woman with a dark ponytail wearing a red coat and a shoulder bag
before: In frame 1 the woman holds the book in her hand at her side.
after: In frame 3 the book is resting on a small wooden stool next to her, no longer held.
change: She lowered the book and put it down on a small wooden stool; the setting shifted from a library to an office with monitors, and her expression went from worried to flat/neutral.
consequence: Unclear, but it suggests she is setting the book aside or giving up on it, moving from the world of books into a work/desk environment; the book is left unread or discarded.
message: The narrator seems to be saying that people put your writing down and move on without reading it (nobody wants to read it).
